## Two points from the literature {#two-sentences-worth-keeping}

::: {.claimcard}
"the common single-path analyses in social and behavioural research should not be simply assumed to be robust to alternative analyses" [@AczelEtAl2026InvestigatingAnalyticalRobustness]
:::

::: {.claimcard}
A blueprint: precise question → causal reasoning (DAG) → multiverse → sensitivity analysis [@AuspurgBruderl2021HasCredibilitySocial]
:::

::: {.small}
- Same-conclusion robustness and same-*number* robustness are different bars
- Justifiability is the criterion – choose with reasons, show the spread
:::

::: notes
The first point comes from the article on the robustness study, which holds that analyses following a single path "should not be simply assumed to be robust to alternative analyses". A single path can be a good one, and the reader is still owed the space around it, so a report needs the chosen path and the alternatives together. Auspurg and Brüderl give the constructive recipe that we followed today: a precise question, assumptions drawn explicitly as a graph, a multiverse and a sensitivity analysis. In your own writing, keep the two standards of robustness apart, the same conclusion, which seventy-four per cent of the reanalyses in the robustness study reached, and the same number, which only thirty-four per cent came close to, and when you claim robustness, say which one you mean.
:::
